clue.text: Sound made by donkeys in holiday islands

indicators.note: the clue asks for the noise a word makes when spoken, so a synonym of donkeys is heard rather than written

parts.note: donkeys are fools or sillies, as in calling someone a silly ass

explanation.surface: Braying donkeys disturb the peace on a holiday island break.
explanation.walkthrough: The Scilly Isles lie off the tip of Cornwall in south-west England and are a popular holiday spot; 'donkeys' means fools, not beach donkeys.
explanation.definitionFit: The Isles of Scilly are a British archipelago visited mainly by tourists, so they are fairly called holiday islands.

clue.text: Train to keep masticating soundly

indicators.note: soundly here means judged by the sound of the words, so the chewing phrase is heard not spelt

parts.note: masticating is chewing, and to keep doing it is to chew, chew

explanation.surface: A command to go on chewing thoroughly, as a parent might give a child.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Soundly' looks like 'thoroughly' but signals a homophone; 'Train' looks like a verb (to teach) but is the nursery word for a locomotive.
explanation.definitionFit: Choo-choo is a child's word for a railway engine, imitating the noise of steam.

clue.text: Lots and lots of punishment

definitions.meaning: a large quantity, as in plenty of cream poured over a pudding
beatings with a whip, the strokes delivered as a penalty

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both abundant amounts in informal British speech and strokes of a whip given as a penalty.

clue.text: Russian's first out of bed

annotationWithheld.why: Russian's first out of bed (4) for IVAN: Russian's first [name] or VAN for first can be seen, but nothing in the clue as held gives the I from 'out of bed'; the clue may be misread and the scan is unreadable

clue.text: True saint in church taking classes in religion

parts.note: CE stands for the Church of England
RE is religious education, a school subject in Britain

explanation.surface: A devout saint attends church lessons on faith in good earnest.
explanation.walkthrough: RE (religious education) is the name for religion lessons in British schools; 'taking' simply joins the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: True and sincere are synonyms when describing heartfelt feelings or a genuine friend.

clue.text: Discoloration in old boats being E scrapped

indicators.note: old boats being broken up for scrap suggests their letters are smashed and rebuilt in a new order
old boats being broken up for scrap suggests their letters are smashed and rebuilt in a new order

explanation.surface: Old hulks broken for scrap show rust marks and stains.
explanation.walkthrough: The stray E is an OCR artefact. 'being scrapped' rearranges IN OLD BOATS; 'in' looks like a link but is part of the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: A bloodstain is a mark that discolours fabric or wood, so it is an example of discoloration.

clue.text: Using computers etc excited solver, so we hear

indicators.note: this phrase tells the solver the words are to be taken as spoken, matching a word spelt differently

parts.note: excited means high, and a solver of mysteries is a detective, TEC in crossword slang

explanation.surface: A crossword solver gets thrilled while using a computer.
explanation.walkthrough: TEC is short for detective, someone who solves crimes; HIGH TEC spoken matches the computer term.
explanation.definitionFit: High-tech describes advanced technology such as computers and electronics.

clue.text: Number of elks, perhaps, surrounding NOUN a wild animal's lair

indicators.note: surrounding tells us the deer go round the outside of what follows

parts.note: elks are an example of deer, hence perhaps
a den is the home of a wild animal such as a fox

explanation.surface: A count of elk herds gathered round a beast's den.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Number' is read as something that numbs (NUM-er), not a count: a deadener dulls feeling. The stray NOUN is an OCR artefact.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that numbs dulls sensation, which is just what a deadener does.

clue.text: Light up entrance to underground tunnel, after trouble

indicators.note: after tells us the letters from the underground tunnel come behind the trouble

parts.note: ill means trouble, as in to speak no ill

indicators.note: the entrance is the opening, so the first letter of the following word

parts.note: a mine is a tunnel dug underground

explanation.surface: Lighting up an underground tunnel's mouth after an accident.
explanation.definitionFit: To illumine is a literary verb for lighting something up or brightening it.

clue.text: Say, prepares to shoot lover that's one over the eight

indicators.note: say here means spoken out, so the next word is to be heard not spelt

parts.note: a gunman cocks a gun before firing
a swain is an old word for a young lover or suitor

explanation.surface: Someone readies a gun for a rival in love who has had one drink too many.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One over the eight' is British slang for slightly drunk, but here it is literal: the cox is the ninth person in a rowing eight.
explanation.definitionFit: In a racing eight the coxswain steers as an extra, ninth member, so is one over the eight rowers.

clue.text: Got down and rested on sofa, perhaps, about middle of afternoon

indicators.note: about means going round, so the sofa word wraps the centre letter

parts.note: to lie on a couch, a sofa being one example, is to have couched

indicators.note: the middle of a nine-letter word is its fifth letter

explanation.surface: Someone took a lie-down on the settee around mid-afternoon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Got down' looks like getting off the sofa but means stooped low.
explanation.definitionFit: To crouch is to bend low with knees bent, so crouched is a synonym of got down.

clue.text: Beast in his corner struggling to take in oxygen

indicators.note: to take in means to hold within, so the jumbled letters enclose the gas symbol
struggling suggests thrashing about, so the letters are thrown into a new order

parts.note: O is the chemical symbol for oxygen

explanation.surface: An animal cornered in its pen gasps for air.
explanation.walkthrough: 'struggling' rearranges HIS CORNER, and 'to take in' puts O inside.
explanation.definitionFit: A rhino is a large horned mammal, a beast in the zoological sense.

clue.text: Half the prefects joining in part of breakfast ritual

indicators.note: joining in means going inside, so the shortened prefects go into the breakfast food

parts.note: cereal is part of a typical breakfast

indicators.note: only half the letters are kept, so the second half of the word is dropped

parts.note: monitors are pupils given authority, like prefects in a school

explanation.surface: Senior pupils join the morning meal as a school ritual.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Half the' keeps only the first four letters of the prefects word; 'joining in' places that inside the breakfast food.
explanation.definitionFit: Ceremonial as a noun means the formal rites of an occasion, a ritual.

clue.text: Poor, resources finally running out

indicators.note: the final letter runs out, so the last letter of the word is lost

parts.note: means are money and resources, as in living within your means

explanation.surface: Someone is poor because their funds have at last run dry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'finally running out' drops the last letter, S.
explanation.definitionFit: Mean can describe something of poor quality or shabby, as in a mean dwelling.

clue.text: Close-shaved hairstyle the fashion? Definitely

parts.note: ton is an old word for the fashion or high society
sure is used as a word of agreement, meaning definitely

explanation.surface: Asking whether a cropped haircut is in vogue, and being told yes.
explanation.walkthrough: TON, from French, means the fashionable world, a crossword favourite.
explanation.definitionFit: A tonsure is the shaved crown worn by monks, a close-shaved hairstyle.

clue.text: Book about passion succeeded in being boring

indicators.note: about means placed around, so the book goes round the other pieces

parts.note: a tome is a large book
ire is anger, a strong passion
S is the abbreviation for succeeded in family trees

explanation.surface: A book about passion managed to be dull.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' sends the book round both other pieces; 'in being' is only a link to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Tiresome and boring are synonyms for something tedious.

clue.text: Important role redesigning one-time apartment

indicators.note: redesigning means remodelling, so the flat's letters are reshaped with one removed

parts.note: T is the abbreviation for time, and one-time means a single T

explanation.surface: A former flat is being remodelled.
explanation.walkthrough: 'one-time' looks like 'former' but means one T, taken out of APARTMENT before 'redesigning' reorders it.
explanation.definitionFit: A name part is the title role in a play, the most important part.

clue.text: I observe church getting flooded?

indicators.note: getting here means receiving round itself, so the flood wraps the church letters

parts.note: a flooded place is under water, so water surrounds it

explanation.surface: Someone watches as the parish church goes under in a flood.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is in the answer's own voice: one who watches might say 'I observe'. 'getting' has the flood surround the church, implied by 'flooded'.
explanation.definitionFit: A watcher is an observer, the one who would say this of themselves.

clue.text: Councillor pursued by journalist, one who's owed money

indicators.note: pursued by means followed by, so the journalist comes second

parts.note: an editor is a journalist in charge of a paper

explanation.surface: A local councillor is chased by a reporter over money owed.
explanation.definitionFit: A creditor is a lender, someone to whom a debt is due.

clue.text: Former member of religious order, not initially an ideal model

parts.note: ex means former, as in ex-wife

indicators.note: not initially means the first letter is dropped

parts.note: a Templar was a knight of a medieval military religious order

explanation.surface: An ex-monk was not, at first, a model person.
explanation.walkthrough: The Knights Templar were a medieval crusading order; 'not initially' drops their T.
explanation.definitionFit: An exemplar is a perfect model or pattern to be copied.

clue.text: Grant for traveller on long journey

definitions.meaning: ... S. Grant was the American Civil War general and president
the Latin name of Odysseus, who wandered for ten years after Troy

explanation.definitionFit: The name belongs both to President Grant and to the Roman form of Homer's wandering hero Odysseus.

clue.text: Capital, partly from equities

indicators.note: partly says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Investment capital drawn partly from shares.
explanation.definitionFit: Rome is the capital city of Italy.

clue.text: Remain wrapped in several sheets after retiring? I might

definitions.text: Remain wrapped in several sheets after retiring? I might

indicators.note: wrapped in means held inside, so the staying word sits within the paper
retiring means going backwards, so the sheets word is read in reverse

parts.note: a ream is a large number of sheets of paper
to linger is to remain

explanation.surface: A shirker stays under the bedsheets after going to bed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'retiring' reads the paper word backwards, giving MAER, and 'wrapped in' puts the staying word inside it; the whole clue then pictures someone feigning illness in bed.
explanation.definitionFit: A malingerer fakes illness to avoid work and might well stay in bed.

clue.text: Singers belting out raps soon

indicators.note: belting out suggests loud, rough treatment, so the letters are battered into a new order

explanation.surface: Vocalists will soon be belting out raps.
explanation.walkthrough: 'belting out' looks like loud singing but rearranges RAPS SOON.
explanation.definitionFit: Sopranos are singers with the highest voice range.

clue.text: Tree on top of mountain is securely rooted

parts.note: a fir is a coniferous tree

indicators.note: in a down clue the top of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A tree on a mountain summit is well anchored.
explanation.definitionFit: Firm means fixed and stable, like something solidly rooted.

clue.text: This fly flutters around one in furtive manner

indicators.note: around means the jumbled letters go round the numeral
a fly flutters about erratically, so the letters are moved about

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A fly darts sneakily around someone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flutters' rearranges THIS FLY, which goes 'around' I.
explanation.definitionFit: Shiftily means evasively, in a way that suggests something is being hidden.

clue.text: What bodysnatchers might do is noble

definitions.meaning: graverobbers dig up and damage a burial plot, so they spoil a tomb
a German title of nobility, like a marquis

explanation.definitionFit: The word reads as two words for damaging a tomb and is also a German nobleman's title.

clue.text: Game introduced by senior's old hat

indicators.note: the game is introduced into the senior abbreviation, going inside it

parts.note: SR is the abbreviation for senior
ombre is an old card game

explanation.surface: An elderly man's old hat, brought out for a game.
explanation.walkthrough: Ombre is a seventeenth-century card game; 'introduced by' puts it inside SR.
explanation.definitionFit: A sombrero is a wide-brimmed Mexican hat.
